$doc: DREDD'S BENCH - every instrument the fleet can convene, what each judges, and how it is run. Dredd (dredd/dredd.mjs) reads this to build a DOCKET for an ask: Jev (TypeSafe's typed-decision model, reached through HSwarm's measured cascade, hswarm_decide) answers each instrument's `jev` question about the ask, and the `keywords` answer the same question when Jev is unreachable. Owner ask (the Chair, 2026-09-21): 'Sometimes the AI may not know which tool to call' - so the tools are named in ONE place, every instrument's own README names this file back, and the judge picks. ADD AN INSTRUMENT HERE and Dredd knows it exists; nothing else needs to change. Fields: `mode` now = Dredd runs it and captures the log; detached = Dredd launches it hidden with a log and names the pid; agent = a skill or an in-session step only the agent can take (Dredd names the exact call); always = part of every docket (recall, delegation, peers). `phase` 1 = facts (cheap, before anyone argues), 2 = the board argues over the facts, 3 = the field (slow, real browsers, real people), 4 = the agent's own follow-through. `{docket}` `{url}` `{ask}` `{checks}` `{surfaces}` `{term}` are filled by Dredd. `owner` says whose lane the findings land in (AGENTS.md § Whose call is it). `plane` says which front door the instrument belongs behind (the Chair, 2026-09-22: 'if it is pretty much deterministic it goes to the Architect; if it has opinions, it goes to Dredd'): architect = a script could decide the answer (same input, same answer), dredd = a model's, persona's or critic's judgment, shared = plumbing every docket uses. `firstSteps` (top level) are fixed FIRST STEP lines a docket prints, whether or not anything convenes, when its domain is the step's `domain` and the ask names one of the step's `when` words (the domain keyword matcher): the step every matter of that shape starts with, where no instrument does it (ruling 2026-09-24, decide-39: the send ledgers for a delivery bug; a ledger-read instrument stays the Chair's call).

firstSteps.note: Read the operator's own rows first: chat email_send_ledger + sms_send_claims, accounts auth_events, events host_event_notifications (the delivery-ledgers instrument runs these reads, filtered to the operator's own identity in the first query), then the trigger's log group via logs_tail.

instruments.name: Page pulse - is it broken?
instruments.judges: Rung one of the page ladder: does the page load at all, with what status, how fast, how many words rendered, any console or page errors, failed requests, broken images, horizontal overflow on a desktop and on a phone, the headlines (h1-h3) and calls to action a skimming reader sees first. Verdict sound | wobbly | broken. A broken page stops the ladder - nothing else about it is worth judging until it loads. It also photographs the page at a desktop and a phone width after a real scroll, whole and then one viewport at a time, and the slices are what rung two scores for a page the Design Critic's capture lane cannot shoot.
instruments.when: Any time a live page is named. Always first.
instruments.jev: Is a LIVE PAGE of the product named or clearly implied, so that its basic health (it loads, no errors, nothing blank or overflowing) should be checked before anything else about it is judged?
instruments.cost: seconds, one headless browser
instruments.evidence: {docket}/page-pulse.json - status, ms, words, errors, overflow, the rendered text, headings and ctas; verdict sound | wobbly | broken. {docket}/page-words.log and {docket}/page-headlines.log for the room; {docket}/page-desk.png and {docket}/page-phone.png, the whole page as an overview, and overlapping viewport slices of each from top to bottom, up to thirty ({docket}/page-desk-01.png, {docket}/page-phone-01.png, ...), which rung two scores one by one

instruments.name: Price check - what does this page cost to read?
instruments.judges: How much attention a page asks of the person on it, in points: every word they read, every control they decide about, every field, card, banner and motion. It names the dearest pages of the repo and the file each point comes from, so a cut aims at the file that earns it. It prices what a page asks of its reader; it does not judge whether the copy is good, the tone right or the backend working.
instruments.when: The ask says a page is too busy, cluttered, too long, confusing or expensive to read, or asks to cut or simplify a page's UI.
instruments.jev: Is the ask about how much a page costs its reader to read or use - clutter, too much on the screen, too long, confusing - so that its price in attention should be measured before anything is changed?
instruments.cost: about twenty seconds, two static scans of the repo
instruments.evidence: {docket}/price.log - the ranked table, dearest page first, with each page's top file; {docket}/price.json - every page's points, units and the file each point comes from

instruments.name: The copy checks
instruments.judges: The words a visitor reads: word economy (Hormozi's cut loop), the volume budget, the recorded cut loop, marketing overclaims and the three forbidden moves, em dashes, AI-writing tells, duplicated copy, and - when a URL is named - page-pulse's read of that page's visible copy (visible words, the longest paragraph, em dashes) from the same load as rung one. The rung is graded from the run's own manifest, never its exit code; the word count is evidence, never a cap, so on an ask about length the rung is the room's call.
instruments.when: Any complaint about copy, wording, length, tone or a page that 'reads like a brochure'.
instruments.jev: Is the person complaining about, or asking to judge, WORDS - copy, wording, headlines, tone, how a page or email reads, or that a page is bloated, too long, verbose or a wall of text?
instruments.cost: free, local, under two minutes

instruments.name: The Humanizer
instruments.judges: AI tells in prose: not-X-but-Y contrasts, staged openers, forced triads, dashes, inflated claims, stock AI words, bold labels, filler. Rewrites without changing what the text says.
instruments.when: After the copy checks name a page, or whenever the complaint is 'this sounds like AI wrote it'.
instruments.jev: Does the ask involve prose that may read as machine-written - stiff, salesy, padded, full of stock phrases - that a rewrite pass would fix?
instruments.run: Skill: humanizer (global skill) over the text the copy checks named
instruments.cost: in-session
instruments.evidence: the rewritten text, in the reply

instruments.name: The Design Critic
instruments.judges: Every declared surface photographed at real viewports and scored against the owner's Material 3 bar by the strongest model in the room (the session itself - never a claude -p subprocess, owner directive 2026-08-08). Issues carry an identity and a state (new / persistent / resolved / regressed) in the issue ledger.
instruments.when: Any complaint about how something LOOKS - layout, spacing, density, hierarchy, colour, a component - and any UI change before it ships.
instruments.jev: Is the person complaining about, or asking to judge, how a PAGE or SCREEN that visitors use LOOKS - layout, spacing, density, colour, alignment, a component, a screenshot - rather than code, tests, tooling or infrastructure?
instruments.needs: nothing running - the wave boots the plane's own -claude dev servers on offset ports (never the owner's :4173), photographs, merges and exits
instruments.then: node {dredd}/dredd.mjs --collect --docket {docket}  (emits the judge worklist; score each PNG in THIS session; design-critic-judge.mjs --ingest <scores.json>)
instruments.cost: a browser per surface, minutes; heavy, so Dredd runs it under fairjob
instruments.anyPage: a page the wave cannot photograph (another host, or another repository judged with --root) is scored from page-pulse's own photographs of it (page-desk.png, page-phone.png) by the vision model at --collect, against the Design Critic's brief and the canon

instruments.name: LilGranny - the first-timer lens
instruments.judges: Findability for someone who has never seen the product: too many choices on one screen, icon-only controls with no words, the thing they came for hidden behind a menu or an overlay. Reads the Design Critic's capture; measured thresholds in the granny engine's header.
instruments.when: Whenever the Design Critic captured, and any complaint that a first-time visitor would be lost.
instruments.jev: Would a first-time visitor who has never seen this product struggle to FIND what they came for on the thing being discussed - too many choices, unlabeled icons, the thing they came for hidden behind a menu or an overlay?
instruments.cost: free, seconds, reads the capture
instruments.evidence: {docket}/lilgranny.log and {docket}/lilgranny/manifest.json or {docket}/lilgranny.json (the second over a page off the roster, read from page-pulse's scan; graded from them, never the exit code)
instruments.anyPage: a page the capture lane cannot photograph (another host, or another repository judged with --root) is graded from page-pulse's own scan of its controls (inventory, mobileInventory) by the granny engine (.arkitect/lib/engines/design-critic/granny-page.mjs), at convene

instruments.name: The Flow Walk
instruments.judges: Every declared multi-step flow driven end to end in a real browser against the flow standard (.arkitect/policies/connections/flow-standard.json): steps, dead ends, the contract each step must meet.
instruments.when: A complaint that a TASK cannot be completed - signup, sign-in, checkout, hosting an event - rather than that a page looks or reads wrong.
instruments.jev: Is the complaint about a multi-step TASK a visitor performs (sign up, sign in, check out, host an event, delete an account) breaking or dead-ending, rather than about how one page looks or reads?
instruments.then: node {dredd}/dredd.mjs --collect --docket {docket}  (reads flow-walk-conformance over this docket's own walk and seats the second sitting)
instruments.cost: a browser per flow on the named page's planes, dev servers booted four at a time, up to four minutes a leg; without a named page it is skipped (the whole fleet, 35 flows, is a hand-run: bun run audit:flow-walk)
instruments.evidence: {docket}/flow-walk.log (the walk) and {docket}/flow-walk-conformance.log (the check over it, read only when the walk finished after this docket launched it)

instruments.name: SUE - simulated people
instruments.judges: What real first-time visitors DO and SAY: each Sue is a real AI session with a persona, a fresh browser, a real inbox and a reason to be there; she never skips a step a human would take, and answers an exit interview in her own words. The Design Critic says the button is the wrong grey; SUE says nobody understood what the button was for.
instruments.when: The complaint is that people do not understand the page, do not know what we sell, or give up - and whenever a public page changes.
instruments.jev: Would sending simulated first-time VISITORS (real AI sessions in a real browser) through a public page or flow of the product answer this - is the question what PEOPLE understand or do on a page, rather than code, tests, tooling, infrastructure or an internal question?
instruments.needs: a brain: convened from a chat, the chat's own agents on Sonnet 5.5, one per Sue (the SUE tier, Owner 2026-10-05, replacing the 2026-09-23 Opus ruling). An unattended hearing has no chat, so SUE sits it out unless the chat pinned a key pool (DREDD_SUE_BRAINS, the Chair 2026-09-23: no API keys unless the chat decides one is needed), and says so plainly
instruments.then: node {dredd}/dredd.mjs --collect --docket {docket}  (status, then the report once every Sue is done, then the second sitting; about two minutes per Sue; DREDD_SUE_COUNT overrides the five)
instruments.cost: real browsers and real model sessions; the cannon self-sizes under fairjob

instruments.name: SUE Focus Group
instruments.judges: What a room of real simulated visitors AGREES is the single biggest problem with a page, argued out loud rather than reported alone: every Sue in the group sees and hears the others' diaries and words, an AI moderator asks what felt off and puts the caller's own suggestions to them only after they have looked for themselves, and the room votes down to ONE agreed problem, with its own quotes. Plain SUE (id sue) gives N independent verdicts; a focus group gives the one thing a room of them would all point at first.
instruments.when: The ask wants ONE agreed answer to what feels off or what the biggest problem is, from a group that can compare notes with each other - not a catalogue of N independent visitors' verdicts (that is plain SUE) and not an argued opinion among the fleet's own critics (that is the Boardroom). Also the fix loop: fix what the last focus group agreed on, then send the next one at the same page to see whether it is still there.
instruments.jev: Would putting several simulated first-time VISITORS in the SAME room, letting them see and talk to each other and converge on the ONE biggest problem, answer this - rather than N independent SUE visits, an argued opinion among the fleet's own critics, or a question about code, tests, tooling or infrastructure?
instruments.needs: a brain: convened from a chat, the chat's own agents on Sonnet 5.5, one per Sue plus one more for the moderator (the SUE tier, Owner 2026-10-05, replacing the 2026-09-23 Opus ruling). An unattended hearing has no chat, so the room sits out, exactly as SUE does, unless the chat pinned a key pool (DREDD_SUE_BRAINS): no tool picks a key pool by itself (the Chair, 2026-09-23)
instruments.then: node {dredd}/dredd.mjs --collect --docket {docket}  (status, then the room's verdict once it closes: the single problem, who agreed, their own quotes; DREDD_SUE_COUNT overrides the default group size)
instruments.cost: real browsers and real model sessions for every Sue plus one more for the moderator; the cannon self-sizes under fairjob
instruments.evidence: {docket}/focus-group.log (the launch and its runId, then, once --collect reads the closed room, what it agreed: the one problem, who agreed and who did not, their own words), sue/runs/<runId>/room/ (verdict.json, the roster and every speaker's lines)

instruments.name: SUE APE - power users (Adversarial Product Evaluation)
instruments.judges: What familiar power users run into: each APE Sue uses this product, or the best one like it, every day, pushes it the fast way (keyboard, Enter, Tab, back, reload, an address typed straight in, undo, a second click) and logs every place it does not work the way it should - what she did, what she expected, what happened. Her exit interview is what broke, which shortcuts failed, what she lost and what to fix first, not what she thinks of the place. A plain SUE is a stranger who forms an opinion; an APE Sue is the regular who has stopped being polite about it.
instruments.when: The complaint is that the product is clunky, slow to get things done in, or does not behave the way it should for people who use it all the time - the regulars, the daily users, the ones who go fast.
instruments.jev: Would sending simulated POWER USERS (familiar people pushing the product hard and fast, real AI sessions in a real browser) through a flow answer this - as opposed to what a first-time visitor understands (plain SUE), one agreed biggest problem (the focus group), code, tests or infrastructure?
instruments.needs: a brain: convened from a chat, the chat's own agents on Sonnet 5.5, one per APE Sue (the SUE tier, Owner 2026-10-05). An unattended hearing has no chat, so the APE Sues sit it out unless the chat pinned a key pool (DREDD_SUE_BRAINS, the Chair 2026-09-23: no API keys unless the chat decides one is needed), and say so plainly
instruments.then: node {dredd}/dredd.mjs --collect --docket {docket}  (status, then the report once every APE Sue is done; about two minutes per Sue; DREDD_SUE_COUNT overrides the default)
instruments.cost: real browsers and real model sessions; the cannon self-sizes under fairjob

instruments.name: SUE ART - designers (Aesthetic Review Team)
instruments.judges: What professional UI/UX designers see when they walk the product: each ART designer walks it on a phone and on a computer, the way a person with one thumb and a deadline would, progressive disclosure first, then the product's other main screens, and hands back a ranked polish list - the screen, what is there now, exactly what to change it to, the principle behind it, and how bad it is (polish, friction or broken) - plus what must be kept. The Design Critic scores photographs of Connections' declared surfaces against the Material 3 bar; ART walks any product's real flows, so it judges layout, states and mobile ergonomics in use.
instruments.when: The complaint or the ask is about polish: the design looks unfinished or amateur, the layout is off or cramped, too much shows at once, the mobile screens are awkward, or the product should be made to look and feel professional and modern.
instruments.jev: Would sending simulated professional UI/UX DESIGNERS (expert reviewers in a real browser, on a phone and a computer) through the product answer this: polish, layout, visual hierarchy, progressive disclosure, mobile ergonomics, states, design consistency, making it look and feel professional and modern - as opposed to scoring screenshots of Connections' declared surfaces against the Material 3 bar (design-critic), what first-time visitors understand (SUE) or what power users run into (APE)?
instruments.needs: a brain: convened from a chat, the chat's own agents on Sonnet 5.5, one per ART designer (the SUE tier, Owner 2026-10-05). An unattended hearing has no chat, so the ART designers sit it out unless the chat pinned a key pool (DREDD_SUE_BRAINS, the Chair 2026-09-23: no API keys unless the chat decides one is needed), and say so plainly
instruments.then: node {dredd}/dredd.mjs --collect --docket {docket}  (status, then the report once every ART designer is done; about two minutes per designer)
instruments.cost: real browsers and real model sessions; the team is three designers, a fixed size

instruments.name: The Architect
instruments.judges: The whole guardrail catalog: every check, gating and advisory, over the repo as it stands. Dredd narrows it to the family the domain names: visual, flow, infra and code quality (dead code, complexity, duplication, AI-writing slop); copy runs through the copy checks' own row, and the strict gate is named for data and the owner runs it once a day - a docket never does.
instruments.when: Anything about code quality, a rule being broken, drift, or 'is this clean'.
instruments.jev: Would running the repository's automated guardrail checks (the Architect: code quality, copy rules, design rules, infra drift) produce evidence for this ask - or is the person asking whether a check, a rule or a tool EXISTS in the repository for something (a word, a dash, a pattern, a style, a drift)?
instruments.cost: seconds per check; the strict gate is minutes and is the owner's time - once a day, never while the tree is moving

instruments.name: The Marketing Council and the minds
instruments.judges: Positioning, offer, pricing psychology and message strategy, argued by simulated named marketers (marketing-council) or one mind at a time: rory (psycho-logic), hormozi (the binding constraint, offers), dunford (positioning), godin, sabri (direct response), chen (network growth), manson, robbins.
instruments.when: The complaint is about what a page SAYS about the product - positioning, the offer, the pitch - not how it is worded.
instruments.jev: Is the ask about POSITIONING, the offer, the pitch, pricing psychology or message strategy - what the product should say about itself, or what a competitor sells and says that we should answer (a competitor teardown) - rather than the wording or the visuals?
instruments.run: Skill: marketing-council (a full session) or one mind: rory / hormozi / dunford / sabri / chen; a teardown of a competitor's site: Skill competitor-profiling on its URLs first (fetch the pages, WebSearch its reviews), then the council over what it found
instruments.cost: in-session; the marketing laws apply (AGENTS.md § pay-rail, the marketing callback hook)
instruments.evidence: the council's write-up, in the reply

instruments.name: The Legal room
instruments.judges: Whether something is legal and what it must say: terms of service, privacy policies, whether a feature is allowed, contracts, marketing claims, AI features, payments and credits, fundraising and investment features, demand and regulator letters. Argued by the Boardroom's built-in counsel (Privacy, Terms, AI & IP, Deal, and General Counsel who rules; Opposing Counsel on the bench), whose playbooks were researched and fact-checked against current primary sources. Ends in a decision (ship / ship with changes / hold), ranked fixes with exact wording, and the part a licensed attorney must still sign.
instruments.when: The ask is a legal question, or work is about to ship something with legal exposure.
instruments.jev: Is the ask a LEGAL question - whether something is allowed, what a terms of service, privacy policy, contract, disclosure or marketing claim must say, a compliance duty, or a demand letter, subpoena or regulator letter - rather than a product, design, code or infrastructure question, or a visitor or customer objecting to, disliking or not trusting something, which is feedback?
instruments.run: Skill: legal-room (this chat thinks each counsel's turn through the Boardroom's own-brain doors, researching live, and writes the lawyer-ready plan into the Legal room's meeting)
instruments.cost: in-session; no Connections AI credits (the own-brain doors)
instruments.evidence: the meeting in the Legal room - its minutes, its plan and its link - in the reply

instruments.name: Project Hydra and the Codex
instruments.judges: Every codebase we own, from one database: which project is stale, what version ships, what the Architect last found, and - through the Codex - which feature or extension point in WHICH product owns a term, with anchors into its code.
instruments.when: Any cross-repo question, anything that names another product, and before touching a product you have not read the brief for.
instruments.jev: Does the ask reach OUTSIDE this repository - another of our products or codebases, the fleet, 'which of our projects', a version or staleness question - so the cross-repo database (Odin) or a product's Codex brief should be consulted, as opposed to reading a competitor's or another company's public website?
instruments.then: python D:/NEWProjects/shared/project-hydra/ph.py codex where <product> {term}  · python D:/NEWProjects/shared/project-hydra/ph.py next · python D:/NEWProjects/shared/project-hydra/ph.py codex brief <product>
instruments.cost: free, milliseconds (SQLite + FTS5)

instruments.name: The Almanac - what the product already has
instruments.judges: What the workspace already HAS for the ask, from the AI's own maintained record (Connections' in tools/almanac, every other workspace's in its memory lane, the same engine reading both): every feature, capability, primitive, guardrail, tool and restructure, per area of the product, with why it exists, its status (live / staged / planned / retired) and its prune verdict. Jev picks the areas the ask is about; every entry of those areas comes back as one line, grouped by kind. It replaced the 22,390-line JUSTIFY_EXISTENCE.md ledger (Owner, 2026-09-28): 'Rather than spending three hours looking through our code base, trying to figure out what we have or don't have ... this is an ever growing list.'
instruments.when: Any ask that needs to know what the product already has before it can be answered: a comparison with a competitor ('are we the best at event hosting, Luma has seven more than us'), 'do we have X', planning or pricing a feature, a gap analysis, where a capability lives after a restructure, or before building anything that might already exist.
instruments.jev: Would knowing what this product ALREADY HAS - which features, capabilities and tools exist in an area, why each exists and whether it is live - help answer this ask: a comparison with a competitor, 'do we have X', whether we are the best at something, planning, pricing or building a feature, or where a capability lives now?
instruments.then: node {connections}/tools/almanac/almanac.mjs area <area> · find <words> · show <id> · prune-queue (the non-KEEP verdicts) · overview (run in the workspace's folder, or the MCP's almanac tool)
instruments.cost: free on disk; one Jev batch (about two seconds) to pick the areas, words when Jev is unreachable

instruments.name: 4man - the foreman's board of work
instruments.judges: What work is waiting, in what order, and who should do it: the one board every AI files tasks on and takes tasks from. Each task carries its project, type, size, the brain it needs, its impact and whether it is live, risky or needs a person; plain code ranks them and routes each to the swarm, a flagship model, a split or the people list, and nothing closes without a passing check or a stated proof. the Chair, 2026-10-01: one massive running collection of to-do items, sorted for an AI, with the AIs deciding and doing the work.
instruments.when: Any ask about what to work on: what is left, what is next, the backlog, the to-do list, what the AIs are working on, what needs a person, filing work that cannot be finished now, or working through open tasks.
instruments.jev: Is this ask about the list of work itself - what is waiting to be done, what to do next, what is left or open, the to-do list or backlog, who is working on what, or filing or taking a task?
instruments.then: node {connections}/tools/4man/4man.mjs next --take --as <you> · show <id> · done <id> · add "<title>" --check "<cmd>" · direction
instruments.cost: free on disk, about a second

instruments.name: AWS Atlas: the bill
instruments.judges: What the fleet SPENDS, read org-wide from the payer account: gross usage, credits and net by month and by account, the last complete month by service (Amazon Bedrock is its own line), the biggest movers, the month projected from its elapsed days, the daily run-rate and its trend, and AWS's own forecast with its interval.
instruments.when: Any money question: the account spend, the AWS bill, credits, a budget, a forecast or month-end projection, what a service, a feature or an AI model costs, tokens burned. The bill goes first on every one of them; the Atlas's map and walk answer what exists and what answers, never what it costs.
instruments.jev: Is the ask about what we SPEND or will spend in dollars - the AWS bill, credits, a budget, a forecast or month-end projection, cost by account, service or feature, or AI model and token spend (Bedrock, a model's credits) - so the org-wide bill would answer it, rather than whether a resource or hostname exists or answers (the Atlas's map and walk), what we charge our own customers (Pay), or a Claude or Codex account's quota?
instruments.then: a spend that moved: name the account and service from the movers, then ask that plane's own Cost Explorer lines under its instance (bun run atlas:who <plane> prints it); an AI or Bedrock line that moved: bun run atlas:ai under Root/Connections - which plane, feature and model spent it, from the ai_spend line every model turn writes, beside the bill's Bedrock lines; which plane spiked yesterday, or what bills every month with next to no traffic: read tmp/money-desk/latest.json (the scheduled Money Desk), or bun run atlas:money -- --daily under Root/Connections for a fresh one (bun run atlas:money alone prints the idle-spend ruling list from the Atlas snapshots, no credentials)
instruments.cost: a few Cost Explorer requests at $0.01 each, free again inside the shared cache window (connections-arkitect/core/cost-explorer-cache)
instruments.evidence: {docket}/bill.log - the rollup (gross, credits and net by month and account, by service, the movers, the projection) and the bill truth (run-rate, trend, AWS's forecast)

instruments.name: Backend performance RSI
instruments.judges: How fast and how costly the BACKEND runs, from the last committed pulses: every Lambda ranked by weekly handler time (warm p50/p90 ms times invocations), GB-seconds and invocations per day, and ACU-hours per day per cluster, beside each function's budget and the lowered budget it could bank (measured plus headroom). The top row is the next thing to fix; a budget far above its measurement is a speedup nobody banked.
instruments.when: Any ask to make the backend, an API, an endpoint or a Lambda faster or cheaper to run, a slow Lambda or endpoint, API latency, cold starts, p50/p90, a latency or performance budget, or 'recursive performance'. What the fleet SPENDS in dollars (the bill, credits, a forecast) goes to the bill; a page that loads slowly in a browser goes to the page pulse.
instruments.jev: Is the ask about how FAST or how resource-hungry our BACKEND runs - a slow Lambda, API or endpoint, latency, cold starts, p50/p90 handler time, invocations, Aurora ACU, a latency or performance budget, or making the backend faster or cheaper to run - so ranking our functions by measured handler time against their budgets would answer it, rather than what we spend in dollars on the AWS bill (the bill), how a page loads in a browser (the page pulse), or a Rust build or test run being slow?
instruments.then: fix the top row at its root cause, deploy it, re-run the pulses under Root/Connections (bun scripts/aws/ops/fleet-latency-pulse.mjs, bun scripts/aws/ops/fleet-acu-pulse.mjs), then bank it: bun run perf:rsi -- --apply in the same change as the fix (.claude/rules/backend-performance-rsi.md)
instruments.cost: free, local, seconds - it reads the committed pulse snapshots; a fresh pulse is a separate CloudWatch read under Root/Connections
instruments.evidence: {docket}/perf-rsi.log - the ranked functions, their measured and budgeted numbers, and the budgets each could bank

instruments.name: The AWS Atlas: who reaches it
instruments.judges: Which AWS identity reaches what an ask is about to touch, read, change or deploy: the plane's own account and the vault instance to pass the Connections MCP, where its DATABASE really lives (26 planes' databases are co-tenants in Studio's account, so the plane's own account is the wrong one there), and the org-management path for fleet-wide reads - derived from the registries the Architect's live checks declare through (plane-capabilities, aurora-cotenants, live-account.mjs), and a hostname or resource found in the Atlas's own fleet snapshots.
instruments.when: Before anything touches, reads, writes or deploys to AWS - a lambda, a bucket, a database or the RDS Data API, logs, a secret or parameter, a migration, a CDK stack, credentials, or which account or vault instance to use. A read under the wrong account does not fail loudly, it comes back empty or AccessDenied. It answers who to be; the Atlas's map and walk answer what exists and whether it answers, the bill what it costs.
instruments.jev: Does the ask involve touching, reading, writing, deploying to or getting access to something in AWS - a Lambda, an S3 bucket, a database or the RDS Data API, CloudWatch logs, a secret or parameter, a migration, a CDK stack, credentials, or which AWS account or vault instance to use - so the first thing to know is which AWS identity reaches it, rather than what it costs (the bill), whether a hostname answers at all (the Atlas's walk), how a page looks or reads, or which AI account (Claude or Codex) has quota left or should take the work?
instruments.then: bun run atlas:who <plane | hostname | account | resource> for one name exactly · pass the named instance to the Connections MCP (instance:) · .claude/rules/deploy-and-aws.md before a deploy or a migration
instruments.cost: free, milliseconds - the registries and the Atlas's fleet snapshots on disk, no AWS call

instruments.name: The AWS Atlas
instruments.judges: Every account, resource and published hostname in the fleet: the fleet map (needs the vault's org credentials), the credential-less outside-in walk (DNS + HTTPS of every published name), drift between the two, and the Architect's three atlas checks. What any of it costs is the bill's (id bill).
instruments.when: Anything about AWS resources, an account, a hostname that is down or does not answer, DNS, a certificate, or 'what is running where'. A money question (the account spend, the bill, credits, a forecast) goes to the bill first.
instruments.jev: Is the ask whether one of our hostnames, sites or APIs is up, resolves or answers at all, or about its certificate or DNS - or about AWS itself (an account, a resource, a deploy, what is running where) - so the fleet map or the outside-in walk would answer it, rather than what any of it costs (that is the bill), what a page shows once it answers (that is the page pulse), a test lane or CI being red (the code gate), or a Claude or Codex account, quota or usage?
instruments.then: bun run atlas:fleet (needs the Connections MCP's org credentials - from a session, never a scheduled task) · bun packages/connections-arkitect/bin/arkitect.mjs --root . --check aws-atlas-walk,aws-atlas-drift --quiet
instruments.cost: the walk is credential-less and a few minutes; the fleet map is longer and reads 31 accounts

instruments.name: Pulse - live product health
instruments.judges: How Connections is actually doing right now, from live telemetry: funnel, activation, retention, revenue (ARGUS) and front-end errors (RUM). Every number names its source; the unmeasurable is flagged, never faked.
instruments.when: A complaint that 'nobody signs up' or 'conversion is bad' - measure before arguing.
instruments.jev: Does answering this need LIVE usage numbers - signups, activation, retention, revenue, front-end errors - rather than a look at the page or the code?
instruments.cost: in-session, read-only, live queries

instruments.name: The security audit
instruments.judges: Auth, tokens, exposure, permissions and RLS, injection: the coverage-led security hunt over the whole repository (a coverage ledger seeded from the tree, one unit per hswarm worker, every candidate refuted before it is reported). The ledger scripts measure; the hunt judges. A single diff or surface gets the built-in security review instead.
instruments.when: Anything that names a token, a leak, a public surface that should not be, or a permission.
instruments.jev: Does the ask involve security - authentication, tokens, credentials, something exposed or public that should not be, permissions or row-level security, an injection?
instruments.run: Skill: security-audit (the whole-repo hunt; a named surface or one diff: the built-in security review)
instruments.cost: in-session

instruments.name: The code gate
instruments.judges: Lint, format and the named tests over the repository paths the ask names - the facts for a CODE ask, without running the whole strict gate (the owner's time). ESLint, Prettier --check, node --test on every *.spec.mjs under the paths, and the bun lane each *.spec.ts belongs to, named, never a bare bun test <dir>.
instruments.when: Any ask that names files, a tool, a module or a directory - including Dredd on itself.
instruments.jev: Does the ask name or clearly concern SOURCE FILES in this repository - a tool, a module, a script, a hook, a test, a directory - so that linting, formatting and running the named tests would produce evidence?
instruments.cost: seconds to a minute, scoped to the named paths

instruments.name: Delivery ledgers - what actually reached the operator
instruments.judges: For a report that a message, code or notification came on the wrong channel, late, or never: reads the OPERATOR's own rows, newest first, over the last 7 days - chat email_send_ledger (every email decision and its From), chat sms_send_claims (by phone fingerprint), accounts auth_events (sign-in and MFA, whose details name the channel) and events host_event_notifications - filtered in the first query to the operator's own identity, never anyone else's. It measures and never judges; which Lambda to logs_tail next is the agent's call from what the rows show.
instruments.when: A delivery report: a text that came as an email, a code or notification that never arrived, a message on the wrong channel.
instruments.jev: Is the ask a report that a message, sign-in code or notification was delivered on the wrong channel, late, or not at all, so that what the send ledgers recorded for the operator would answer it?
instruments.cost: seconds, five read-only queries under the Studio host instance
instruments.evidence: {docket}/delivery-ledgers.json - the operator's ids, emails and phones, and each ledger's rows (or its error); {docket}/delivery-ledgers.log, one count line per ledger

instruments.name: CodeGraph and the codemap
instruments.judges: Where a symbol lives, who calls it, and what a change must touch - deterministic, for about 600 tokens instead of a recon agent.
instruments.when: Any 'where is X' or 'what calls X' before a code change.
instruments.jev: Does the ask need to LOCATE code - where a symbol, route, handler, table write or file lives, who calls it, what a change would touch, where something is persisted or stored (a person who cannot find a button or a link on a page is not asking where code lives)?
instruments.run: codegraph_explore { question } (MCP) · codegraph explore "<question>" · python ~/.claude/tools/codemap.py check
instruments.cost: milliseconds
instruments.evidence: the symbol's source and callers, in the reply

instruments.name: The Script Vault
instruments.judges: Whether an enumerator already exists for the sweep you are about to hand-run. Search first, run it with script_run, save a proven one with script_save.
instruments.when: Any 'find all X' / 'check every Y'.
instruments.jev: Is the ask a SWEEP - find all X, check every Y, count, enumerate across the codebase or the fleet - that a saved script may already answer?
instruments.run: connections_search_catalog { query } → connections_execute { local:true, tool_name:"script_run", params:{ script, args } }
instruments.cost: milliseconds to search

instruments.name: Rust build, test and check time
instruments.judges: Why a Rust repository is slow to build, test or check, measured rather than guessed: how many test programs each crate links (every tests/*.rs is its own compile, link and PDB), which repo's pinned compiler lags the newest stable, and which git worktrees are merged, clean and idle.
instruments.when: Any complaint that cargo build, cargo test, clippy or a Rust gate takes too long, and before bumping a Rust toolchain.
instruments.jev: Is the ask about a RUST codebase being slow to build, test, lint or check (cargo, rustc, clippy, a Rust CI gate), or about which Rust compiler version a repo uses?
instruments.then: python ~/.claude/tools/rust_test_merge.py <crate> [--keep a,b] merges a crate's test files into one program; rust_toolchain_sync.py --apply bumps lagging pins (then the repo's own gate); worktree_audit.py --remove clears merged idle worktrees, moving their tmp/ evidence first
instruments.cost: seconds, read-only until a fix command runs
instruments.evidence: each tool's own output: test programs per crate and what blocks merging them; floats / current / LAGS per repo; removable worktrees
instruments.doc: claude-memory global/one-test-executable-per-crate-is-the-rust-build-lever.md and global/every-rust-repo-runs-the-newest-stable.md; the Architect check rust-test-executable-sprawl

instruments.name: The memory lane (recall)
instruments.judges: Which of the fleet's memories this ask needs. The lane is the notes plane's pgvector store (Titan v2 embeddings, HNSW, cosine) holding every file of Lunarwerx/claude-memory by (repo, slug) - the 'right proper vector database' already exists; Dredd queries it (memory_search) for every docket.
instruments.when: Every docket.
instruments.run: memory_search { query, limit } via the local MCP
instruments.cost: one embedding, milliseconds

instruments.name: The memory ledger (who reads and who changes each memory)
instruments.judges: Which memories to improve, from use rather than opinion. The notes plane's memory ledger (schema 0056) records who read each memory and who changed it, with the text a change replaced, and works out the leads: memories still unread two weeks after they were saved, ones rewritten three or more times, a project filed under two spellings, a project whose memories nobody read in 30 days. The owner reads the same numbers on the CrAInium's Lexicon tab (the Chair, 2026-10-02: 'not just pretty pictures, but so you can recursively improve things').
instruments.when: An ask about memory, the knowledge base or the Lexicon, or a memory that looks stale, wrong or missing from the cloud.
instruments.jev: Is the ask about the AIs' stored memories or knowledge base: whether they are used, current, filed right, or in the cloud at all?
instruments.then: verify a lead's memories that still hold (memory_verify) and prune the rest (memory_prune { unread_for_days, dry_run: true } first); save a split project's memories under one spelling; one memory's whole history is bun scripts/memory/memory-ledger.mjs --id <slug>; a memory missing from the cloud is saved there with memory_save (memory_search first: the slug is an upsert key)
instruments.cost: one ledger read through the local MCP, a few seconds
instruments.evidence: the ledger's per-project counts and leads, printed to the instrument's log

instruments.name: The team board and the mail (peers)
instruments.judges: Who else is working on this: the team board (every AI on the project, on every machine; claims, private threads) and this folder's mail on the same board (one AI leaves another folder's AI a note). Dredd reads both so the docket names a peer already on it, and can announce a convened docket with --announce.
instruments.when: Every convened docket.
instruments.run: board_who · board_read · board_read { box: "all" } via the local MCP; board_post to announce
instruments.cost: milliseconds

instruments.name: Is the AI message board being used (CrAInium)
instruments.judges: Whether the fleet uses the shared message board the way the owner intends, in his own words: AIs post to a shared message board, other AIs see those boards, together they build a large repository of notes, knowledge, memories and comments, AIs talk to each other directly when needed (AgentHydra: "go check the message board"), and message each other live. Cranium pulls the account's throughput numbers, a cheap model judges them against the owner's five behaviours (judge only from the numbers, name the number behind every claim), and the verdict lands in one HTML page.
instruments.when: An ask about whether the AIs use the message board, memory or talk to each other, or about the board's throughput.
instruments.jev: Is the ask about whether the AIs USE the message board - posting, seeing each other's boards, building shared knowledge and memories, talking to each other directly or live - or about its throughput, rather than a request to send one board message?
instruments.cost: one cranium call and one hswarm ask; seconds

instruments.name: HSwarm (delegation)
instruments.judges: How the work is delegated: ALL delegated subtasks (research, code, review, judgment, per-item sweeps) go through HSwarm, selected by published benchmarks per task profile (code / decision / general); the desktop Opus 5.5 orchestrates and final-decides. The tier (DELEGATION) only shapes it: hswarm = bulk of delegated subtasks; mixed = desktop judgment over HSwarm subtasks; flagship = the desktop's own final synthesis, no desktop workers; opus_lean = only an explicit access/capability fallback after suitable HSwarm routes are exhausted, with a recorded why-not-hswarm reason. On quota/credit failure try other capable and then stronger Swarm configurations; desktop only for documented unavailable capability/access. An instrument that names its own tier keeps it only on a why-not-hswarm access gap (MODEL: SUE on Opus 5.5 for its local MCP access), never on price. Policy: skill hswarm-routing.
instruments.when: Every docket.
instruments.run: hswarm_run { cwd, tools, tasks } · hswarm_ask { prompt } · hswarm_decide { items }
instruments.cost: free pool first, then cents
instruments.doc: hswarm/README.md in the AgentHydra repo, skill hswarm-routing

instruments.name: The Grid
instruments.judges: The whole backend as squares - what is red, what was last run, where things stand - read from the artifacts the lanes already wrote; a status nobody measured renders never-run, never green (owner directive, Owner, 2026-09-19: the repo at a glance).
instruments.when: Any 'how are we doing', 'what is red', 'where do things stand' ask about the repository as a whole.
instruments.jev: Is the ask about the overall state or health of the repository right now - what is red, what was last run, where things stand across the board - rather than about one page, one file or one feature?
instruments.cost: seconds, reads artifacts

instruments.name: The Subtraction Lens
instruments.judges: Whether a thing should exist at all: ranked question, delete, simplify, automate last, over the Architect's could-be-smaller checks (owner directive, the Chair, 2026-08-13: the most valuable thing you can do is cut dead weight).
instruments.when: The ask is 'should this exist', 'cut the dead weight', 'what can we delete' - never 'fix it' or 'build it'.
instruments.jev: Is the ask about whether something should EXIST at all - cutting dead weight, deleting, simplifying, removing what is unnecessary - rather than fixing, judging or building it?
instruments.cost: minutes - it runs the subtraction family of checks; hidden with a log
instruments.evidence: {docket}/subtract.log (its progress lines), tmp/audits/SUBTRACTION.md (the ranked report it writes)

instruments.name: The Architect Board
instruments.judges: One page over every instrument's latest numbers - the design critic per surface, the checks, the mobile checker, Lighthouse, the looked-at ledger, a per-plane rollup - each labelled with when it was measured.
instruments.when: Before running anything new: what did the instruments already say, and when?
instruments.jev: Is the person asking what an instrument LAST SAID and WHEN - the design critic's latest scores for some pages, the checks' last results, Lighthouse, what was last looked at - so one page of the most recent numbers answers it without running anything new?
instruments.cost: seconds, reads artifacts, writes one HTML page (never opens a window from a docket)

instruments.name: AgentHydra - the fleet's quota
instruments.judges: What every Claude and Codex account has left, which instance this session is, whether a fan-out is safe, and where heavy work should be routed (check_my_usage, list_usage, usage_budget).
instruments.when: Any ask about the AI fleet's own usage, quota, rate limits, accounts or which session should take the work.
instruments.jev: Is the ask about the AI fleet's OWN quota, usage, accounts, rate limits, or which account or session should do the work - rather than about the product or its code, or what anything costs in dollars (that is the bill)?
keywords: how much do we have left
instruments.cost: milliseconds, no quota
instruments.doc: skill hydra-status, the agenthydra MCP instructions

instruments.name: The deep codebase audit
instruments.judges: A nine-lens semantic sweep no linter can do - dead code, bespoke vs library, DRY, fault propagation, performance, conditionals, legacy, intent - grounded against the Architect's settled decisions and adversarially verified; report only.
instruments.when: The ask is a broad 'is everything doing its job', not one file or one rule.
instruments.jev: Is the ask a BROAD semantic audit of the whole codebase - dead code, bespoke copies of library things, duplication, fault propagation, legacy - rather than one file, one page or one rule?
instruments.run: Skill: deep-codebase-audit (hswarm workers hunt and refute, you synthesise; report only, you decide what to apply)
instruments.cost: in-session plus one hswarm batch per phase
instruments.evidence: the audit report, in the reply

instruments.name: The code review
instruments.judges: One CHANGE - a branch, a diff, what is about to land - read by the reviewers whose paths it touches (dredd/reviewers/*.md, or the judged repository's own .dredd/reviewers/): the Standards judge (the repository's own rules for those paths, then a twelve-smell baseline, every smell labelled a judgement call) and the Spec judge (missing, scope creep, wrongly built, each quoting the ask) always sit, and a specialist sits when one of its `@ref glob:` lines matches a changed path. The two axes are never merged; a coordinator in code dedupes within each, grades by a rubric that leans toward approval, takes a dismissal only with its disproof (`<kind>:<citation>` in an inline `dredd-review-ignore:` or `--dismiss`, the citation checked before any model, never on a critical or escalating finding, which is refused with its owner) and returns one verdict: approve, approve_with_comments or request_changes.
instruments.when: A review of a change rather than a page or a product call: before a merge, after a landing, or when someone asks whether a branch does what was asked and follows the rules.
instruments.jev: Is the ask a review of a code CHANGE - a diff, a branch, a pull request, or work about to be merged or just landed - asking whether it is correct, follows the repository's rules, or builds what was asked?
instruments.cost: free to think (one hswarm call per seated reviewer, usually three or four); under a minute
instruments.evidence: {docket}/review.md (the Standards and Spec axes under their own headings, the worst finding on each) and review.json (the verdict, every finding with its id:<fingerprint>, what was suppressed and why)

instruments.name: Dredd's hunt - the judge's own measured failures
instruments.judges: What the judge itself gets wrong, as measured, never argued: the gold asks the newest eval convened wrong, the instruments that failed or exited 0 without their evidence in the last dockets, the decision changes no A/B measured, the rooms that seat more critics than a brief needs, the instruments no gold ask names, and anything the doctor calls missing - ranked, each with its one action (lib/hunt.mjs). Read-only and deterministic: no model call.
instruments.when: The ask is about Dredd itself - what the judge gets wrong, what it convenes or seats, its bench, dockets, eval or hearings - so a room arguing over the judge argues over its measured failures, not only a lint log (the Chair, 2026-09-23).
instruments.jev: Is the ask about Dredd itself (dredd, the judge that picks which instruments to convene and which critics sit) - its logic, bench, dockets, seats, eval or hearings - rather than about something Dredd is asked to judge?
instruments.cost: seconds, no model call: it reads the doctor, the last 60 dockets, the newest eval run, the A/B ledger and git

instruments.name: Chat audit - what the operator typed and where the hours go
instruments.judges: The operator's OWN chats on this machine, measured by script: every prompt he typed (extract_prompts.py, AI replies and hook text stripped), what he repeats, complains about and re-explains (friction_scan.py), how long each turn really takes and what eats it (turn_times.py, tool_sinks.py, request_latency.py), and what the hooks cost (hook_costs.py). The numbers are the evidence; reading the prompts for themes is judgment on top. His transcripts are private: they stay on this machine and on Claude agents, never HSwarm.
instruments.when: The ask is about the operator's own work pattern: what he keeps saying or complaining about across his chats, burnout, where his time or the chats' time goes, what to automate next so he stops doing it by hand (Owner, 2026-09-24: 'go through all of my chats... what is he doing that's causing burnout').
instruments.jev: Is the ask about the OPERATOR'S OWN chats or work pattern - what he keeps saying, repeating or complaining about across his AI chats, where his hours or the chats' time go, burnout, or what to automate so he stops doing it by hand - rather than about the product, a page or its code?
instruments.run: python %USERPROFILE%/.claude/tools/chat-audit/turn_times.py --days 14 · extract_prompts.py then friction_scan.py (what he typed) · tool_sinks.py · hook_costs.py - all in %USERPROFILE%/.claude/tools/chat-audit (source: claude-memory home/tools/chat-audit)
instruments.cost: a minute or two of local python over the transcripts, no model call; theme reading on top is Claude agents only (private transcripts)
instruments.evidence: the scripts' printed summaries and their JSON beside them, quoted in the reply
